This fixes the issue reported in this comment: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14851#issuecomment-3863896385

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI


def s_start():
    print("SYNC START", flush=True)


app = FastAPI(on_startup=[s_start])
```

        func if is_async_callable(func) else functools.partial(run_in_threadpool, func)  # type:ignore

                async with AsyncExitStack() as function_stack:

steps.message: The fix was to move the initialization of `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown` in `APIRouter.__init__` to occur after the call to `super().__init__`, preventing the parent class (`starlette.routing.Router`) from overriding these attributes and erasing user-provided handlers.

The bug was caused by `APIRouter.__init__` initializing `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown` before calling `super().__init__`. Since the parent class `starlette.routing.Router` also initializes these attributes, the user-provided handlers were being overwritten. Moving the assignments after the `super().__init__` call ensures that the user-provided handlers are preserved and correctly executed by the lifespan context.
